draftNote: 3 of five queued off a bottom-two lane: Goldilocks324 (jungle→midlane), Cuban Noobster (offlane→carry), Xeebs (support→jungle).

coaching.headline: Lt. Belica's rotation answered an early two-kill hole, and kills finished fourteen to six with both Fangtooths and the Genesis Core. A proper fucking beating.
coaching.team: Sevarog killed Greystone twice before the team scored, and Lt. Belica answered the second from mid 22 seconds later for the team's first kill. The kill count was level at two and again at four apiece. From there the team took ten of the last twelve kills. The team also took both Fangtooths, the Genesis Core, fourteen river buffs to six and two enemy outer towers while losing one. The only Fangtooth or Prime objective the enemy got was the Mini Prime, taken with nobody on the team dead.

focus.title: Turn won fights into objectives
focus.action: After a won fight, one player calls the nearest live objective or enemy structure and the team walks there together. When the Mini Prime is up and enemies are on death timers, the Prime is the call, ahead of chasing another kill.

19.call: Two plays on opposite sides of the map. Sevarog killed Greystone on the offlane and the allied offlane outer tower fell soon after. On the duo lane, Murdock killed Serath and Lt. Belica rotated in from mid to kill Neon, and the team then took the enemy duo lane outer tower and the second Fangtooth.

13.7.call: Two separate picks on opposite sides of the map, not one fight: GRIM.exe killed Murdock on the duo lane and Mourn killed Greystone on the offlane. That drew the enemy level at four apiece, and the team took the first Fangtooth shortly after.

15.8.call: Lt. Belica killed Mourn and Wukong killed Neon, with no allied deaths. The fight went 2-0, and the enemy took the Mini Prime in the same stretch with nobody on the team dead.

22.2.call: Two plays on opposite sides of the map. Greystone killed Sevarog on the offlane. On the duo lane, Murdock killed Serath and GRIM.exe, and Neon killed Steel. The team then took an enemy outer tower and the Genesis Core.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Murdock was broke for a carry: two completed items, the fourth-most gold on the team and farm under the Murdock norm. Between fights, Murdock takes the nearest safe wave so Vanquisher and Imperator land before the next big fight.
Mr_Meat31 still turned GRIM.exe into a piñata: three kills on GRIM.exe, one death all game, the most kills in the game and the most hero damage on the team.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Zero deaths, the most objective damage in the game and both Fangtooths to the team. Goldilocks324 ran a clean fucking jungle on Wukong, and Serath finished without a single kill.

Wukong cleared four enemy wards, every clear the team got, and placed one. Before every Fangtooth and Prime contest, Wukong sweeps the pit approach if a sentry is equipped and calls a laner to ward the entrance.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Sevarog killed Greystone three times, first blood included. A shit exchange rate and the most deaths on the team. When Subjugate lands, Greystone stays inside the zone until the chain breaks; leaving it means a stun.
Still, Cuban Noobster ate the most damage and did the most healing in the game on Greystone, then took down Sevarog in the final fight. Real meat-wall numbers.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy Guggenheim left an unopened mid twice for kills on the offlane and duo lane, died zero times, finished the richest player in the game, and mid never lost a structure. Filthy, greedy, correct.

Hero damage per minute still sat under the recorded Lt. Belica norm with all that gold. Neon stacked mana with Azure Core and Combustion, so Lt. Belica parks Void Drone on Neon before firing Neural Disruptor.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Proper support shift from Xeebs on Steel: tied for the most assists in the game, a hand in over a third of the team's kills, wards above the recorded Steel norm and the second-most damage mitigated on the team.
Mourn placed the most wards in the game and Steel cleared none. When the duo wave is shoved, Steel spends that window sweeping the duo-side river for Mourn's wards, with a sentry if one is equipped.

matchup: GRIM.exe's basic attacks deal magical damage, Energy Shield blocks the next ability, and Instant Reload lets GTFO execute and recast.
Murdock killed GRIM.exe three times for one death to him, and the allied duo never died before ten minutes.
When Energy Shield goes up, Buckshot goes first so Long Arm of the Law is not the ability blocked.
build: Lightning Hawk and Tainted Rounds both add critical chance and attack speed, feeding the charged Shots Fired attack.
Tainted Rounds cuts healing against Serath, second in healing, and Mourn's Contagion heals.
Neither item adds armor or health against a mostly magical enemy team.
eternal: Vermis and Serration add maximum- and missing-health damage on every third hit, suited to finishing GRIM.exe and Serath.
Melting Point only pays above a high physical armor threshold; only Sevarog and Mourn carried physical armor items.
Breach is the second-minor alternative, shredding armor after an ultimate hit for Wukong and Greystone's follow-up.
augment: Justice's Reach makes the charged Shots Fired attack pierce and reach further, past minions or a frontliner.
Sting Operation is the alternative: two more Static Trap charges and larger traps, more roots against divers.
crest: Pacifier's Adrenalize dashes and empowers the next physical hit, harder on low-health targets, with a recast after a kill.
Murdock's basic attacks, Buckshot and Long Arm of the Law are all physical, so the empowered hit always lands something.
improvement: The winning core is Lightning Hawk, Vanquisher and Imperator; Murdock finished Lightning Hawk and Tainted Rounds only.
If Greystone keeps Tainted Blade and Steel keeps Tainted Guard, anti-heal is covered and Tainted Rounds is the slot to compare.
With five kills and one death, no build impact is proven either way.

matchup: Serath vanishes and dashes to a target with Heaven's Fury, then dives with Ascend, which Crushing Descent makes stun.
Serath built Sky Splitter and Spectra for sustained basic-attack damage with lifesteal.
Serath finished without a kill and with the second-most healing in the game.
build: Manta Scythe adds attack speed, lifesteal and bonus damage on isolated targets.
Infernum burns maximum health, harder against bonus armor, and Sevarog and Mourn carried physical armor items.
Wukong carried no magical armor against four magical damage dealers.
eternal: Lotus grants small random bonuses on a timer and on takedowns, and Early Bloom grants an extra level.
Immaculate cuts damage taken near full health, so it fades once a fight starts biting.
Masterpiece is the first-minor alternative, trading the free level for damage and speed that grow with kills.
augment: Masterful Mimicry adds a clone and generates Hair stacks on a timer, so the ultimate spawns clones without every stack from hits.
From Up High is the alternative, trading clone pressure for a bigger Body-stance slam.
crest: Nex's Reap dashes, damages and slows nearby heroes, harder with the Sow charge from recent hero damage.
Land basic attacks and abilities on a hero before pressing Reap; its penetration stacks with Manta Scythe and The Perforator.
improvement: The winning core is Manta Scythe, Infernum and Syonic Echo; Wukong built The Perforator instead of Syonic Echo.
Syonic Echo trades armor penetration and a slow for lifesteal and post-cast attack speed; Dread is the magical armor comparison.
With zero deaths and the most objective damage in the game, the build is a sound keep.

matchup: Sevarog fears with Phantom Rush, chains with Subjugate and stuns anyone leaving the zone, and knocks back with Colossal Blow.
Sevarog built health, physical armor and self-healing, and every Sevarog ability deals magical damage.
Sevarog killed Greystone three times, first blood included; Greystone killed Sevarog once.
build: Overlord cleaves around the target and grows health from kills.
Tainted Blade cuts healing on Greystone's physical damage, aimed at Sevarog's Fist Of Razuul heal and Serath's lifesteal.
Neither item adds armor, and Stoicism's armor is physical only, no help against Sevarog's magical abilities.
eternal: Krix adds maximum health and size; Voracity and Cannibalism feed health from unit kills and takedowns.
Regenerative Tissue is the first-minor alternative, recovering health between trades with Sevarog.
Feeding Frenzy is the second-minor alternative, adding attack speed per nearby enemy hero for faster Overlord cleaves.
augment: Tainted Oath makes Sacred Oath apply Blight, overlapping with Tainted Blade, which already blights on physical hits.
Close Cut is the alternative, making Make Way hit harder in close trades with Sevarog.
crest: Saphir's Mantle's Atlas grows Greystone's size and maximum health, damages nearby heroes and adds permanent health.
It also adds a little of both armors, the only magical armor Greystone carried against Sevarog.
improvement: The winning core is Overlord, Rapture and Aegis Of Agawar; Greystone finished Overlord and Tainted Blade only.
Aegis Of Agawar scales armors by a percentage, but with no magical armor item it has little to scale.
Mistmeadow Buckler for Tainted Blade adds magical armor and a magical damage block; Tainted Oath, Tainted Rounds and Tainted Guard keep anti-heal.

matchup: Neon dashes with Erase Vector, slows with Data Burst, and Overclocks every basic ability during Final Thread.
Neon built Azure Core, Combustion and Overseer, so Final Thread hits harder and heals Neon on hero damage.
Lt. Belica killed Neon once and Neon never killed Lt. Belica.
build: Combustion and Wraith Leggings add area damage, magical penetration and bonus damage on low-health heroes.
Noxia pays maximum-health damage when a second ability follows, so Seismic Assault into Void Bomb or Neural Disruptor.
Lt. Belica completed the full winning core; no enemy completed a magical armor item.
eternal: Aion grants mana regeneration on casts and gold from spell damage, a fit for the game's richest player.
Bottomless Vial adds magical power and a potion charge per river buff Lt. Belica personally kills, rewarding her own river takes.
Sacrifice is the first-minor alternative, refilling mana on ability hits and kills instead of river-buff power.
augment: Combat Veteran pays experience every second plus a little movement speed, speeding up maxed abilities through Innovation.
Pulsefire Rounds is the damage alternative, adding on-hit damage to SMG fire between casts.
crest: Soulbearer's Anima shields Lt. Belica and adds magical lifesteal and movement speed, turning a spell rotation into sustain.
With zero deaths it is a sound keep; Epoch is the draft alternative only if Sevarog or Serath start reaching Lt. Belica.
improvement: With no enemy magical armor items, the next slot leans toward raw damage like Oblivion Crown over more penetration.
Oblivion Crown raises magical power by a percentage, aimed at hero damage per minute under the Lt. Belica norm.
A defensive slot only earns a place if Phantom Rush and Subjugate start catching Lt. Belica.

matchup: Mourn pulls with Abduct, mesmerizes with Beguile, heals allies, shreds both armors with Contagion and darkens vision with Eclipse.
Mourn built Dynamo and Golem's Gift and placed the most wards in the game.
Steel killed GRIM.exe once, and Neon got Steel's only death in the final fight.
build: Xenia shields a nearby ally and adds both armors, the only completed allied item with magical armor.
Dynamo amplifies damage on immobilized enemies, which Shield Bash and Shield Slam stuns trigger.
Tainted Guard cuts healing and bleeds basic attackers, aimed at Serath's lifesteal and Sevarog's heal.
eternal: Krix adds maximum health and size; Regenerative Tissue and Cannibalism add recovery and permanent health from takedowns.
Festering Wounds is the first-minor alternative, but three Tainted items already covered anti-heal, so Regenerative Tissue stays.
augment: Heavy Metal adds armor-scaled magical damage to Heavy Punches and Shield Bash; Xenia, Dynamo and Tainted Guard each add armor.
Adaptive Force is the alternative: two Force Shield charges and a shorter cooldown, but smaller walls against ranged projectiles.
crest: Sanctification's Safeguard shields Steel and nearby heroes, with tenacity against Beguile's mesmerize and Phantom Rush's fear.
It also pays passive gold, raises the ward cap and gives diminishing minion gold.
improvement: The winning core is Xenia, Dynamo and Gaia Greaves; Steel built Tainted Guard instead of Gaia Greaves.
Gaia Greaves trades anti-heal and bleed for a little more health and Tremor movement stacks; neither adds magical armor.
With one death and the second-most damage mitigated on the team, the build is a sound keep.

threats: Chain-CC risk (1 hard-CC abilities, ~0.5s of lockdown): Mourn Abduct (pull). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Mourn. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 3 items of it.
Enemy is 4/5 magical — one magic-resist item goes a long way.
Dive threat on our backline: Serath. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Static Trap root → Buckshot → Hot Pursuit AS → Long Arm of the Law global snipe
ourKits.winCondition: trap for the root, then out-range with Shots Fired and finish with the global ult
ourKits.passive: every 5th basic is a long-range bonus shot
ourKits.playWith: frontline/peel to protect his low mobility
ourKits.playAgainst: almost no escape — engage past the trap and he dies

ourKits.combo: Windsurge engage → Cyclebreaker damage-reduction spin → clones from 84000 Hairs
ourKits.winCondition: stance-dance for damage or tankiness and overwhelm with clones
ourKits.playWith: a team that fights alongside his clones
ourKits.playAgainst: AoE clears his clones; CC him during the damage-reduction window

ourKits.combo: Assault The Gates leap → Make Way armor shred → Sacred Oath empowered basic → Stone Forged Soul stasis ult
ourKits.winCondition: front-line aggressively and reset the fight with the stasis heal
ourKits.playWith: a team that fights while he soaks and stasis-resets
ourKits.playAgainst: don't waste burst into his stasis — wait it out; anti-heal cuts the ult heal

ourKits.combo: Seismic Assault knockup → Void Bomb → Neural Disruptor silence ult, Void Drone mana drain
ourKits.winCondition: knock up + silence a target and burst with missing-HP scaling
ourKits.playAgainst: dodge Seismic Assault; she's immobile — dive when ult is down

ourKits.combo: Bull Rush knockback → Force Shield wall → Shield Slam knockup+stun ult, Shield Bash %hp
ourKits.winCondition: peel the carry with walls/knockups or engage with Shield Slam
ourKits.playWith: a carry he can wall for and peel
ourKits.playAgainst: his Force Shield blocks projectiles — reposition around it; bait Shield Slam

enemyKits.combo: Energy Shield block → Displacement Blast → Assault Mode → GTFO lockon ult
enemyKits.winCondition: out-trade with Pulsefire and the spell-shield, finish with GTFO
enemyKits.playWith: peel so he can free-cast in Assault Mode
enemyKits.playAgainst: bait Energy Shield, then commit; dodge GTFO's slow channel

enemyKits.combo: Ascend dive → Heaven's Fury multi-strike → Chastise slow → Heresy form ult, resets on takedowns
enemyKits.winCondition: dive the backline and snowball Heresy resets
enemyKits.playWith: a frontline that creates her dive angle
enemyKits.playAgainst: peel the backline — deny the first kill and her resets dry up

enemyKits.combo: Abduct pull → Contagion ally-heal bugs → Beguile damage-reduction → Eclipse vision-denial ult
enemyKits.winCondition: pull a target in and sustain the team through the brawl
enemyKits.playWith: burst that punishes his pulled target
enemyKits.playAgainst: respect the long Abduct channel/range; anti-heal blunts Contagion

enemyKits.combo: Phantom Rush → Subjugate root → Siphon → Colossal Blow
enemyKits.winCondition: stack Souls to snowball Siphon and lock down with the root
enemyKits.passive: ability kills grant permanent Soul stacks (HP + damage)
enemyKits.playWith: a team that converts his root into kills
enemyKits.playAgainst: deny his last-hits early to starve Souls; dodge the slow Subjugate

nemeses.playAgainst: Do not walk out of Subjugate while chained, since leaving stuns you; wait it out. Contest his last hits early to slow his Souls, and position so Colossal Blow cannot knock you into his team.
